theme: Offline-first apps: local changes, instant feedback and queues

terms.definition: A design where the app works from local data first and talks to the server when it can.
terms.example: An offline-first app never shows a blank screen.
terms.code:
var local = ["note": "draft"]
let online = false
local["note"] = "edited"
if !online { print("saved locally") }

terms.definition: Showing a change on screen right away, before the server confirms it.
terms.example: An optimistic update makes the like button feel instant.
terms.code:
var liked = false
liked = true
let serverOK = false
if !serverOK { liked = false }
print(liked)

terms.definition: A waiting list of changes saved on the device, which the app sends to the server later.
terms.example: The sync queue sends the edits when we are online.
terms.code:
var queue: [String] = []
queue.append("edit note 1")
queue.append("delete note 2")
for job in queue { print("send:", job) }
queue.removeAll()
terms.output:
send: edit note 1
send: delete note 2

video.description:
Learn to explain how an app keeps working without a connection: Offline-First, Optimistic Update & Sync Queue, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Offline-First - A design where the app works from local data first and talks to the server when it can.
Optimistic Update - Showing a change on screen right away, before the server confirms it.
Sync Queue - A waiting list of changes saved on the device, which the app sends to the server later.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Offline-First, Optimistic Update and Sync Queue in English?

dialogue.title: Like it, even offline
dialogue.setting: Making the like button work offline

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the like button waits for the server. On a bad network, it feels broken.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Make the app offline-first. It works from local data first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the user can like a post without internet?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Use an optimistic update. Show the like right away, like `liked = true` in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But what if the server says no?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then you roll the change back. An optimistic update is a bet that the server will agree.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And where does the change go while we are offline?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Into a sync queue, like `queue` in our code.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So the sync queue is a waiting list of changes?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. When `online` is true, the app sends them and clears the sync queue.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I forgot to clear it, so some posts were liked twice.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good catch. Offline-first needs a clean sync queue after every send.

dialogue.code:
var queue: [String] = []
var liked = false
let online = false
liked = true
queue.append("like post 7")
if online { queue.removeAll() }
